Bitwise to Liquidate Dogecoin ETF BWOW, Trading to End October 14

Bitwise announced that it will liquidate and close its Dogecoin ETF (NYSE: BWOW). The fund is expected to cease operations after its final trading day on October 14, 2026, with creations of new shares also ending. Remaining shareholders will receive a cash distribution on October 22 based on the fund’s net asset value as of October 21, with no action required. Bitwise said the liquidation is part of an adjustment to its product lineup. — link

August 2026 Exchange Derivatives Volume Report: total $3.51 trillion, MoM increased 15.9%, futures/spot decreased 2.6%

WuBlockchain data shows that derivatives trading volume across major crypto exchanges reached $3.51 trillion in August, up 15.9% MoM. Binance ranked first with $1.67 trillion and a 47.7% market share, followed by OKX at $636.6 billion and Bybit at $312.8 billion. The top three exchanges accounted for 74.7% of total volume. The futures-to-spot volume ratio fell 2.6% MoM to 6.87x from 7.06x in July. — link

Coinbase Partners with Moov to Bring Stablecoin Services to 1,000+ Community Banks and Credit Unions

Coinbase has partnered with payments infrastructure provider Moov to provide more than 1,000 community banks and credit unions served by Moov with stablecoin payment acceptance, settlement and real-time funding through Coinbase’s stablecoin payments infrastructure, custodial wallets and Payments API. Use cases include consumer payments, merchant acceptance, merchant settlement and payouts, without requiring the institutions to build their own crypto infrastructure. — link

Former Bank of England Deputy Governor Jon Cunliffe Joins Fnality as UK Chair

Former Bank of England Deputy Governor Jon Cunliffe has joined blockchain wholesale settlement firm Fnality as chairman of its UK operating entity, according to Bloomberg.

Former Bundesbank payments chief Jochen Metzger has also joined Fnality Europe’s supervisory board and is expected to become its chair. Backed by institutions including Goldman Sachs, UBS, Santander, Bank of America and Citi, Fnality is seeking regulatory approval to launch dollar and euro versions of its institutional wholesale payment system. —

Nasdaq Invests $100M in Kraken Parent Payward at $21 Billion Valuation

According to Bloomberg, Nasdaq is investing $100 million in Payward, the parent company of cryptocurrency exchange Kraken, through its venture investment arm. The capital injection values Payward at $21 billion and deepens a strategic partnership established between the two firms in March, according to people familiar with the matter. The collaboration aims to accelerate the buildout of next-generation market infrastructure designed to support the trading, settlement, and custody of tokenized equities. — link

U.S. Treasury Triples Long-Bond Buyback to $6 Billion as Yields Hit Multi-Year Highs

The U.S. Treasury will buy back up to $6 billion of 10- to 20-year Treasuries on Sept. 10, triple the size of its previous long-dated operation, as part of plans to expand buybacks and improve liquidity in the world’s largest sovereign bond market. The move follows a bond selloff that pushed 30-year yields to their highest since 2007; yields continued rising after the announcement, with the benchmark 10-year yield reaching 4.8528%, its highest since November 2023. — link

Arthur Hayes Publishes FLOP Network v0.5.0 Draft, Targets Q4 Testnet

Flop Labs CEO and BitMEX co-founder Arthur Hayes released a draft of the FLOP Network v0.5.0 yellow paper, outlining an AI inference metering and settlement network built on Substrate/FRAME with BABE block production and AlephBFT finality. The project’s roadmap targets a testnet launch in Q4 2026, with token airdrops tied to test participation, followed by a mainnet launch in Q1 2027. The yellow paper remains a draft, with several parameters and mechanisms still subject to change. — link
